note: The Governor of Svalbard's page on entry and residence (updated 7 January 2025, read 2026-10-30): although Svalbard is part of Norway, the Immigration Act does not apply there, and foreigners need no visa, work permit or residence permit from the Norwegian authorities to go there. Everyone staying must meet the Regulations relating to rejection and expulsion of persons from Svalbard, among them having the means to live there, and the Governor may turn away anyone who doesn't; that condition isn't held. A Schengen visa is still needed to travel through mainland Norway by whoever needs one for the Schengen Area (the visits engine's matter).

sources.title: The Governor of Svalbard (Sysselmesteren), Entry and residence
sources.said: Although Svalbard is part of Norway, the Immigration Act does not apply to the archipelago. ... Foreigners do not need a visa or work and residence permits from the Norwegian authorities to travel to Svalbard. ... Among the requirements is that you must have the means to be able to reside on Svalbard.
